title: Section 93 — Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it

content.overview: BNS s. 93 — Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it. BNS restatement of IPC 317. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 317. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 93 is the rule on “Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it”. The section provides that whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 93 exists so that “Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve years of age, by parent or person having care of it” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
93. Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both

Explanations
Explanation.—This section is not intended to prevent the trial of the offender for murder or culpable homicide, as the case may be, if the child die in consequence of the exposure

learningObjectives: Master the elements of exposure and abandonment of a child under twelve years of age under BNS s. 93.
Identify the special duty-bound perpetrators: father, mother, or guardian having care and custody.
Understand the Explanation preserving liability for murder or culpable homicide if death ensues.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 93 provides that whoever, being the father or mother of a child under the age of twelve years, or having the care of such child, shall expose or leave such child in any place with the intention of wholly abandoning such child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Imposes strict penal liability on parents and guardians who breach their fundamental duty of care by exposing or abandoning young children to the elements or public hazards.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 93 (corresponding to IPC s. 317).
Perpetrators: Father, mother, or any person having the care of a child under twelve years.
Actus reus: Exposing or leaving the child in any place.
Mens rea: Intention of wholly abandoning the child.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to seven years, or fine, or both.
Explanation: Does not prevent the trial of the offender for murder or culpable homicide if the child dies in consequence of the exposure.
essentialIngredients: The child is under the age of twelve years.
The accused is the father or mother of the child, or a person having the care of such child.
The accused exposed or left the child in any place.
The act was done with the intention of wholly abandoning the child.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 93 enforces parental and custodial responsibility over young children under twelve years of age. The offence requires two physical acts: 'exposing' (placing the child in a situation of physical peril, cold, or neglect) or 'leaving' the child in any place, combined with the specific mens rea of intending to wholly abandon the child (severing all parental custody and protection). Temporary leaving without intention to wholly abandon does not satisfy s. 93. If the abandoned child perishes from starvation, exposure, or wild animals, the statutory Explanation ensures that the offender can be prosecuted for murder (s. 103) or culpable homicide (s. 100), rather than escaping with the seven-year penalty of s. 93.
examples: Teaching example (Abandonment in a forest): A parent leaves an eight-month-old infant in an isolated dense forest with the intention never to reclaim the child. Passersby discover the child alive. The parent is liable under s. 93.

Teaching example (Exposure resulting in death): A guardian leaves a three-year-old child in an abandoned building in freezing winter temperatures intending to abandon it; the child dies of hypothermia. Under the Explanation, the guardian can be tried for murder or culpable homicide.
distinctions: Section 93 vs Juvenile Justice Act provisions: Section 93 is a specific penal provision for parents/custodians wholly abandoning children under 12; JJ Act provisions broadly address cruelty, neglect, and abandonment across all minor ages.
Section 93 vs Section 94: Section 93 applies to living children under twelve exposed or abandoned; Section 94 applies to secret disposal of a dead body to conceal birth.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a father who left his five-year-old child on a railway platform and boarded a departing train after packing the child's clothes and writing a note stating he gives up all claims to the child is liable under s. 93.
Rule: A parent leaving a child under twelve with intention of wholly abandoning it commits an offence under BNS s. 93.
Application: The child was five years old, the accused was the father, and the intention to wholly abandon was proven by the note and conduct.
Conclusion: The father is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 93.

Perpetrators are strictly parents or persons having care/custody.
Requires intent to wholly abandon the child.
If the child dies, the accused may be prosecuted for murder or culpable homicide.
